summary: This document describes the requirements and implementation of a group telephony feature known as Bridged Line Appearance, Multiple Line Appearance, or Shared Call Appearance, using SIP. Several phones can share one address and see the calls on it.

eli5.summary: In an office, several phones can show the same line, so anyone can see if it is busy and pick up. This explains how to do that with internet phone calls.

questions: what is an appearance agent in sip
how does sip call pickup work
subtitle: How several SIP phones can share one address, see each other's calls, and pick up or join them.

tldr.problem: Business telephony expects several phones to share a line, show the state of its calls and let any member answer, pick up or join a call. SIP has no concept of lines.
tldr.mechanism: Phones share a SIP Address of Record. An Appearance Agent hands out appearance numbers and reports call state through the SIP dialog event package, extended with new elements and an Alert-Info parameter.
tldr.outcome: Phones from different vendors can show consistent call state and use Replaces and Join to take or bridge calls. The RFC updates RFC 3261 and RFC 4235.

today: RFC 7463 is a Proposed Standard. It updates RFC 3261 and RFC 4235, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Shared Lines in SIP
sections.content:
This RFC describes a group telephony feature known as Bridged Line Appearance (BLA), Multiple Line Appearance (MLA) or Shared Call/Line Appearance (SCA). In SIP, where there are no lines, it is called shared appearances of an Address of Record (AOR).

Several user agents (UAs) share a common AOR, learn about calls placed and received by the others, and pick up or join calls in the group. The design uses standard SIP, SIP events (RFC 6665) and publication (RFC 3903), carrying the dialog state event package of RFC 4235.

An appearance number keeps the old telephony idea of a numbered line: users expect it ("Joe pickup line 3") and it is a useful basis for the user interface. Each AOR has its own numbering space.
sections.eli5: Think of an office phone with several numbered buttons. Everyone with the same kind of phone sees the same buttons light up, and a call stays on the same numbered button for everybody.

sections.title: Usage Scenarios and Requirements
sections.content:
The RFC lists four scenarios: an executive and assistant who share calls, a call group such as an IT help line, a single line extension where one answer informs the other phones, and a user changing from one UA to another mid-call using the appearance number.

It then sets 16 requirements, REQ-1 to REQ-16. Key ones are that incoming calls are offered to a group and any member can answer; each UA can learn the call status of the others; a UA can join or pick up a call securely; minimal configuration is needed; and the mechanism must scale. Each call gets a common appearance number from a managed pool, with contention resolved. A UA that does not know the feature must still be able to register and make and receive calls.

Further requirements cover privacy (appearance information must not leak outside the group), exclusivity (a UA can ask for a private conversation), and seizure (reserving an appearance number before sending the INVITE).
sections.eli5: The rules say: anyone in the group can answer, everyone can see who is busy, calls keep their number, outsiders cannot snoop, and you can ask for a private call.

sections.title: The Appearance Agent and Operation
sections.content:
Many requirements are met with existing SIP: a forking proxy and registrar offer calls to the group, the dialog package reports state, and Replaces and Join move calls around. The new piece is the Appearance Agent, a single point of control for the shared appearance resource, like a focus in conferencing. It can be part of a central server or sit in a member UA.

A complete system has UAs that support the extensions, an Appearance Agent built on a dialog package State Agent, a forking proxy that can talk to it, and a registrar that supports the registration event package.

On start-up a UA registers against the AOR, then subscribes to the dialog package of the AOR. If the subscription fails, no Appearance Agent exists and the feature is not active. The UA MAY retry at intervals no shorter than four hours. Incoming calls fork to all UAs, and the appearance number arrives both in a NOTIFY and in the INVITE itself, so a lost NOTIFY does not leave a UA guessing. If the two conflict, the NOTIFY wins.
sections.eli5: One helper, the Appearance Agent, keeps the list of which buttons are in use. Phones ask the helper when they start, and the helper tells everyone when something changes.

sections.title: Seizing, Selecting, Picking Up and Joining
sections.content:
An appearance can be seized before a call by publishing an artificial "trying" state, or merely selected, in which case the number is learned after the INVITE. The assigned number is generally the smallest positive integer not already in use for that AOR.

If a UA needs a particular appearance number, it MUST send a dialog package PUBLISH and wait for a 2xx response before the INVITE. This applies when the user seizes a number, asks for no appearance number (for example a consultation call), joins a call, or replaces a call. An emergency call MUST NOT wait for confirmed seizure.

To bridge or take a call, the UA first publishes the appearance number of the target call plus its dialog identifiers in <joined-dialog> or <replaced-dialog>, then sends the INVITE with Join or Replaces. Publishing first stops the Appearance Agent assigning a new number by mistake.

During a transfer the appearance number should not change, to avoid a jump in the user interface. If the transferee is the shared-group UA, it SHOULD publish to move the number from the old dialog to the new one before sending BYE.
sections.eli5: Before taking a call or reserving a button, a phone says so out loud first. That way the helper does not hand the same button to somebody else by accident.

sections.title: Dialog Package Extensions and Alert-Info
sections.content:
Four new sub-elements of <dialog> extend the dialog package, defined in the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:sa-dialog-info.

  • <appearance> carries the appearance number. A UA sends it in a PUBLISH with state "trying" to request a number; the agent sends it in a NOTIFY to say it was assigned.
  • <exclusive> is a boolean hint that the UA will not accept a Join or Replaces for the dialog. A proxy MAY enforce it with a 403 (Forbidden).
  • <joined-dialog> lists dialogs mixed with this one. Joined dialogs share an appearance number.
  • <replaced-dialog> lists dialogs replaced by this one, which also share the number.

The appearance parameter on the Alert-Info header field is defined as appearance-param = "appearance" EQUAL 1*DIGIT. A UA MUST NOT insert it; only the Appearance Agent or its proxy does. There MUST NOT be more than one per header, and the parameter SHOULD be removed before the INVITE leaves the group. The UA recognises the feature by the shared Event header field parameter, as in Event: dialog;shared.
sections.eli5: The phones add little extra notes to their status messages: which button, whether it is private, and which calls are joined together.

sections.title: How the Appearance Agent Behaves
sections.content:
The Appearance Agent MUST implement a dialog package State Agent for the UAs registered against the AOR and MUST support publications and subscriptions. It MUST be able to discover the state of all dialogs of the AOR, using the registration event package to find the UAs and subscribing to their dialog state if needed.

It MUST allocate an appearance number for every incoming call and notify subscribers at once. A new number is allocated unless the INVITE carries Join or Replaces, in which case the number of the target dialog is reused. It SHOULD send notifications when a call is received, placed, answered or ended, put on or off hold, joined or replaced, and when a number is reserved or released.

A PUBLISH with an invalid number gets a 400 (Bad Request) and an immediate NOTIFY with full state. A number can belong to only one dialog unless joined or replaced dialogs are indicated. A PUBLISH without an appearance number but with the shared parameter means the UA wants none, which policy may refuse with a 400. In the early dialog state the agent controls publication refresh through Expires, with 3 minutes RECOMMENDED. The number stays allocated until the last associated dialog ends, and is freed at once if the call is forwarded to another AOR.
sections.eli5: The helper gives each new call the lowest free button, tells everyone, and takes the number back when the last call on it ends.

sections.title: User Interfaces and Non-Shared Phones
sections.content:
Phones differ, so the RFC gives guidelines. A single-appearance UA still uses number "1" and SHOULD reject other appearances with 480 (Temporarily Unavailable) or 486 (Busy Here). A dual-appearance UA uses "1" and "2". A fixed-appearance hard-phone rejects calls outside its configured range, while softphones with variable numbers should keep a consistent order by appearance number, not arrival order.

State is rendered as idle, active or hold. Hold is detected from the +sip.rendering=no feature tag on the local target URI.

A basic UA with no knowledge of appearances can still join the group if the proxy cooperates with the Appearance Agent. If it does not support Join or Replaces, its dialogs SHOULD be marked exclusive. This interoperability is not required, so it is not available in every deployment.
sections.eli5: Simple phones with one button just show button 1 and ignore the rest. Fancy phones show all the buttons in number order.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Security considerations of SIP and the event framework apply. NOTIFY and PUBLISH bodies MAY be encrypted end to end with S/MIME, or sent over TLS for hop-by-hop confidentiality. All SUBSCRIBEs and PUBLISHes between UAs and the Appearance Agent MUST be authenticated. Without that, a third party could learn dialog details and use them to hijack or manipulate calls.

Because the feature relies on Replaces and Join, an INVITE carrying either MUST only be accepted from a peer that has been authenticated by a standard SIP mechanism such as Digest or S/MIME, and is authorized to request the replacement. Otherwise a third party could disrupt or hijack dialogs in the group. Emergency calls MUST NOT wait for seizure confirmation.
sections.eli5: Only people who prove who they are may look at the call list or grab a call. Otherwise a stranger could steal your calls.
